summary: AI observability has become critical as LLM deployments scale, enabling teams to trace prompts, monitor costs, detect failures, and evaluate output quality in production. The LLM observability platform market reached an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and is projected to hit $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, with Gartner predicting it will account for 50% of GenAI deployment investments by 2028. Without proper observability, teams fly blind on runaway API costs, latency regressions, and quality degradation across complex multi-step agent workflows.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chains, agents, prompt versions, evaluation runs, and dataset-driven regression tests primarily within the LangChain ecosystem
features: Rich trace and span debugging for LangChain and LangGraph workflows
Prompt versioning and management
Dataset creation and evaluation harnesses
Human feedback annotation and scoring
Online monitoring with alerting on latency and error rates
Integrated playground for prompt experimentation
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage ~$2.50 per 1,000 traces; Enterprise custom pricing. Approximately £80/month for 100K traces.
tools.best_for: Teams heavily invested in LangChain or LangGraph who need the richest debugging, evaluation framework, and prompt management in a tightly integrated workflow

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per request, latency, error rates, and user-level spend across multiple providers via a proxy gateway
features: One-line proxy setup requiring minimal code changes
Best-in-class cost tracking and spend dashboards
Multi-framework and multi-provider support
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and bucket-level controls
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month with compliance features; Enterprise custom. Approximately £20/month for 100K traces.
tools.best_for: Cost-sensitive teams wanting the simplest possible setup with the best cost visibility and optimization across any LLM provider

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM traces, evaluation runs, prompt experiments, model inputs and outputs, and dataset versioning alongside traditional ML training metrics
features: Unified platform bridging ML training tracking and LLM observability
Weave tracing for multi-step LLM and agent pipelines
Experiment-style evaluation workflows with scorers
Dataset and artifact versioning
Prompt and model comparison across runs
Integrations with major LLM frameworks and providers
Collaborative team dashboards
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Team plans start at $50/user/month; Enterprise custom pricing. Usage-based components apply for large-scale trace volumes.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams already using W&B for model training who want a unified platform covering both classical ML experiments and LLM evaluation without adopting a separate tool

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM spans and traces, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, embedding drift, model performance, hallucination signals, and enterprise-scale telemetry across ML and LLM workloads
features: Span-level tracing extending long-standing ML monitoring into LLM workloads
Arize Phoenix for open-source local and self-hosted observability
RAG retrieval evaluation with relevance and groundedness scoring
Experiment-style workflows for offline evaluation
OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation support
Embedding visualization and drift detection
Enterprise governance and audit logging
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AI managed platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth and Enterprise plans are custom-priced based on span volume and features.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing comprehensive telemetry that spans both traditional ML model monitoring and modern LLM observability, especially for complex RAG systems

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, cost per trace, latency, custom evaluation scores, and user session flows
features: Detailed LLM tracing with nested span support
Prompt management with versioning and A/B testing hooks
Custom score hooks for online and offline evaluations
OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
Dataset management for regression testing
Open-source and fully self-hostable
Integrations with OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, and more
tools.pricing: Langfuse Cloud free for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud tiers start around £20/month for higher volumes; Self-hosted costs approximately £30/month in infrastructure plus ~2 hours maintenance/month; Enterprise custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams wanting flexible tracing and prompt management with the option to self-host for data privacy, fitting naturally into OpenTelemetry-native stacks

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token counts, latency, and request metadata via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation across multiple LLM providers and frameworks
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK for automatic LLM instrumentation
Drop-in integration requiring minimal code changes
Compatibility with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend such as OpenObserve, Jaeger, or Datadog
Support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and major frameworks
Standardised semantic conventions for LLM spans
Vendor-agnostic by design, avoiding lock-in
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free to use. Costs depend only on the observability backend chosen to receive the telemetry data.
tools.best_for: Teams that want vendor-agnostic, standards-based LLM instrumentation and prefer to route telemetry into their existing OpenTelemetry infrastructure rather than adopting a dedicated SaaS platform

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: LLM traces and spans, infrastructure logs, application metrics, distributed traces, and frontend RUM in a single unified deployment
features: Unified LLM observability combined with full infrastructure monitoring
Prompt tracing and cost tracking alongside logs and metrics
OpenTelemetry-compatible ingestion
Real user monitoring for frontend applications
High-compression storage making it significantly cheaper than Elasticsearch at scale
Self-hostable with a managed cloud option
Dashboards and alerting across all telemetry types
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free; Cloud managed tier starts with a generous free tier and pay-as-you-go pricing based on ingestion volume; Enterprise custom pricing available.
tools.best_for: Teams tired of maintaining separate DevOps telemetry and LLM observability stacks who want a single deployment covering infrastructure, applications, and AI workloads together

tools.name: Confident AI
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination rates, answer relevancy, faithfulness, bias, toxicity, and comprehensive evaluation metrics integrated directly into the observability layer via DeepEval
features: 50+ evaluation metrics open-sourced through DeepEval
Evaluation-first observability combining testing and production monitoring
RAG evaluation including contextual precision and recall
Regression testing pipelines with dataset management
Online evaluations running automatically in production
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft
CI/CD integration for quality gates before deployment
tools.pricing: DeepEval is open-source and free; Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier for small teams; paid plans are custom-priced based on evaluation volume and team size.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritising output quality and safety evaluation who want the deepest evaluation metric coverage in the industry, especially for RAG pipelines and agent reliability

cost_tips: Implement request-level caching using tools like Helicone or a Redis layer to serve identical or semantically similar prompts from cache, which can reduce redundant API calls by 20-40% in applications with repetitive query patterns

Audit and compress your prompts regularly by reviewing traces in tools like Langfuse or LangSmith to identify bloated system prompts, unnecessary few-shot examples, or verbose context being sent on every request — trimming token counts directly reduces per-call costs

Use model routing to match task complexity to the cheapest capable model, sending simple classification or extraction tasks to smaller models like GPT-4o Mini or Claude Haiku while reserving expensive frontier models only for tasks that genuinely require their capability

Set budget alerts and per-user rate limits using cost monitoring tools like Helicone or Arize so you catch spending anomalies before they compound, and enforce token output limits on completions to prevent runaway generation costs from unbounded max_tokens settings
